Then any subsequent `flush()` — explicit `Flush`, `Close`, rollover, or `Optimize`'s `dump()` — takes the full path: persist memory blocks, commit the version, remove the WAL, and the promotion at `collection.cc:1538–1548` can no longer orphan data. An equivalent-target alternative is to change the gate at `segment.cc:2220` to test actual dirty state (e.g. `memory_store_ != nullptr` / writing-block `doc_count_ != 0`) instead of handle presence; a defensive guard in `switch_to_new_segment_for_writing` (fail if a dumped writing segment's meta still has no persisted blocks covering its in-memory `doc_count()`) would turn any future variant of this bug from silent loss into an error.
